question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 40% on the cost price of an article after giving three consecutive discounts of 5%, 10% and 15% to a customer. What would have been the profit percentage, had the shopkeeper given discounts of 5% and 10% only?
solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper earns a profit = 40% on the Cost price of an article

The three discounts = 5%, 10% and 15%

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

SP = MP × (100 – Discount%)/100

CP = 100/(100 + profit%) × SP

**Calculation:**

Let MRP be Rs. x

A shopkeeper earns a profit of 40% on the cost price of an article.

If CP = 100 then, SP = 140

Discount on MRP = 5%, 10%, and 15%

SP = MRP × ({{100-D₁}over100})× ({{100-D₂}over100})× ({{100-D₃}over100})

⇒ 140 = x × ({{95}over100})× ({{90}over100})× ({{85}over100})

⇒ x = (140× 100× 100× 100)over(85 × 90×95) = 192.64 (Approx)
